subsystems.name: Growing structure
subsystems.role: stacks plants in many tiers inside a sealed, insulated building to multiply yield per square metre of land.

subsystems.name: Lighting
subsystems.role: replaces sunlight with tuned LED spectra, since no daylight reaches the inner tiers.

subsystems.name: Root-zone delivery
subsystems.role: supplies water and dissolved nutrients directly to roots with no soil.

subsystems.name: Climate control
subsystems.role: holds temperature, humidity and CO2 at set points in a dense, sealed canopy.

subsystems.name: Sensing and control
subsystems.role: continuously measures the crop and adjusts light, water and air.
parts: temperature, humidity, CO2 and EC/pH sensors

subsystems.name: Power and heat
subsystems.role: delivers the large electrical load and removes the heat that lights and dehumidifiers produce.

buildSteps.title: Site the facility
buildSteps.detail: Choose a site next to cheap, firm low-carbon electricity and near the consumers — power, not land or sunlight, is the limiting resource.

buildSteps.title: Build the sealed envelope
buildSteps.detail: Erect an insulated, sealed building with the structural loads and headroom needed for many stacked tiers.

buildSteps.title: Install racking and root-zone plumbing
buildSteps.detail: Assemble growing racks, then fit troughs or misters, pumps, dosing units and recirculation pipework.

buildSteps.title: Fit lighting
buildSteps.detail: Hang LED arrays at the spacing each crop needs and provide cooling or heat recovery, because most input electricity becomes heat.

buildSteps.title: Commission climate control
buildSteps.detail: Tune HVAC, dehumidification and CO2 dosing so the dense canopy does not become saturated and stagnant.

buildSteps.title: Add automation
buildSteps.detail: Install conveyors, robots and machine vision for seeding, transplanting, monitoring and harvesting.

buildSteps.title: Trial crops
buildSteps.detail: Start with leafy greens and herbs, which tolerate dense canopies and fast cycles, before attempting fruiting or staple crops.

buildSteps.title: Scale out in modules
buildSteps.detail: Replicate the proven module near other population centres; only then does the idea approach metropolitan or planetary scale.

prerequisites.why: when sunlight is removed, electricity becomes the main feedstock and dominates running cost.
LEDs convert electricity to usable photons with little waste heat compared with older lamps.
sealed, high-density canopies need continuous dehumidification and airflow to avoid disease.

prerequisites.tech: Robotics for planting, tending and harvesting
prerequisites.why: hand labour does not scale economically to large automated facilities.

prerequisites.tech: Crop varieties bred for dense indoor canopies
prerequisites.why: field varieties were selected for sunlight, spacing and weather, not for stacked artificial light.

pathway.milestone: commercial vertical farms supplying leafy greens, herbs and seedlings to nearby cities
pathway.unlocks: short, reliable supply chains for perishable greens, independent of weather.

pathway.milestone: profitable production of higher-value crops such as berries, tomatoes and plant-derived compounds
pathway.unlocks: premium markets that can absorb the energy cost.

pathway.milestone: integration with very cheap or curtailed renewable power and waste-heat reuse
pathway.unlocks: lower operating costs and a smaller carbon footprint per kilogram of food.
a real contribution to feeding metropolitan populations — but only if electricity and automation become far cheaper than today.

food security in places with almost no arable land or water; it would need dedicated generation on the scale of large power grids, so it stays a niche tool rather than a replacement for field agriculture.
